summary: Full-text technique dossier: the Middle Run-Through (MRT), the Tampa-2 middle linebacker's hardest job, walked through one Blake Cashman rep against Buffalo. author: @_avichawla
title_or_hook: NVIDIA Dory: the looped transformer, VERIFIED at arXiv, and the post gets three facts wrong
summary: Dory1.0-4B (arXiv:2611.03998, Fishman et al., NVIDIA, submitted 2 Nov 2026, VERIFIED at the primary source this run): a 4B-parameter looped (latent-recurrent) language model on a normalized-GPT backbone; an input block, a shared recurrent block, and an output block, where the recurrent block can be applied a variable number of times at inference (elastic depth). The paper reports pre-training on 6 trillion tokens (the first 4.5T in NVFP4), context extended to 256K, then SFT and RLVR post-training with a difficulty-aware loop curriculum; with two or more loops it outperforms larger models (Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, Gemma 4 26B-A4B named) on average across 12 benchmarks, and with four loops it generates 1.3-2.5x fewer tokens on agentic benchmarks. Checkpoints are open-sourced (BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, GGUF). The thread errs on three points: it claims 14T training tokens (paper: 6T), describes a two-part main-plus-loop KV cache (paper: keys and values are cached only from the last loop), and names Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen3 8B as the beaten baselines (paper: Qwen3.5-9B and the Gemma 4 family). All performance claims are the paper's own benchmarks, UNVERIFIED independently.
engine_training_value: None directly, context only for the engine. For the routing stack, the trainable asset is the loop-count-vs-accuracy curve on fleet tasks, which the first test would produce.
provenance: Primary source arXiv:2611.03998 (Fishman et al., NVIDIA); poster @_avichawla is the explainer/recreator, and the thread errs on three points corrected in the dossier.
source_section: F2 - NVIDIA Dory: the looped transformer (@_avichawla)

A brief is a piece of work that edits files no other piece touches; a session is one agent working one brief; the harness routes each brief to a seat, checks the goal file fast, and runs a verifier that reads the actual files after every edit. The pattern closely mirrors the fleet's existing discipline, so the dossier books it as a portable checklist (file-disjoint by construction, verifier reads actual output files, cheap goal check per task).
